description: AICPA frameworks for reporting on controls at service organisations. Not regulations but widely required by customers and auditors.

issuing_bodies.name: American Institute of Certified Public Accountants
issuing_bodies.remit: US accounting standards body; publishes SOC engagement standards and the Trust Services Criteria.

standards.name: SOC 1 — Reports on Controls at a Service Organization Relevant to User Entities' ICFR
levels: Type 1 (point-in-time), Type 2 (over a period, typically 6-12 months)
standards.summary: Report on controls relevant to user entities' internal control over financial reporting (ICFR). Driven by SSAE 18 (US) or ISAE 3402 (international equivalent).
key_principles: Type 1: description and design of controls at a point in time
Type 2: design + operating effectiveness over a period
Intended for financial reporting audit purposes

standards.name: SOC 2 — Reports on Controls Relevant to Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, or Privacy
standards.summary: Report against the Trust Services Criteria (TSC). Security is mandatory; other four categories are optional based on scope.
key_principles: Trust Services Criteria — Common Criteria (security) is always in scope
Optional categories: Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, Privacy
Type 2 is the version most commonly required by enterprise customers

standards.name: SOC 3 — General Use Report
standards.summary: Public-facing version of SOC 2. Shorter, omits detailed control descriptions and auditor test results; suitable for marketing and public distribution.
key_principles: Auditor's opinion on Trust Services Criteria
No disclosure of detailed controls or test procedures
Often accompanies a SOC 2 report — both produced from the same audit
